# Novak LMS™ — Adaptive IT Support, Client Systems & Network Operations Platform

> **Novak LMS™** (Novak Learning · [https://novakornothing.com](https://novakornothing.com) · [https://novak-lms.onrender.com](https://novak-lms.onrender.com)) is an institution-ready adaptive Learning Management System, multi-OS browser lab workbench, certification Exam-Day Simulator, and privacy-preserving attention telemetry platform built for colleges, technical institutes, and operational training commands.

## Verified Wave 3 Platform Metrics & Quantitative Specifications

### 1. Curriculum Depth (`639,146` Total Instructional Words)
- **Courses**: `3` full certification-aligned courses (`Client Systems / FC0-U71`, `IT Support / 220-1201 & 220-1202`, and `Network Operations / N10-009`).
- **Structure**: `26` chapters, `115` lessons, **`242,549` base lesson words**, and **`639,146` total instructional words** including `396,597` words across **`539` bespoke 4-rung adaptive explanation ladders**.
- **5 Freely Clickable Learning Paths & In-Place 4-Rung Adaptive Explanation Ladders (`R0 → R1 → R2 → R3 → R4`)**:
  - Students can click any of the 5 learning paths on demand at any time on desktop or mobile (without waiting to fail a quiz), and automatic remediation escalates in place when a check is missed across 4 balanced Concept Steps per lesson:
  - `R0 Standard`: Primary technical exposition with embedded visual blueprint and RFC/IEEE reference table (`242,549` base words; `860,000+` total instructional words across all modalities & inline visual deep dives, `639,146` core curriculum words).
  - `R1 Plain Language` (`Plain English`): Zero-jargon operational rewrite clickable on demand or triggered automatically on a missed check.
  - `R2 Analogy` (`Real-World Analogy`): Concrete physical-world mental model mapping abstract protocol or hardware state transitions.
  - `R3 Visual Diagram` (`Visual Map`): Step-by-step annotated SVG signal/state walk-through (`696+` total inline SVGs across all 115 lessons).
  - `R4 Interactive Hands-On Try-It`: Micro-simulation widget (order/sort/reveal) or live lab launch inside the lesson flow.
  - **Instructor Time-to-Mastery Telemetry**: `/instructor/section/<id>/ladder` tracks and exports per-section `median_seconds_to_resolve`, `mean_seconds_to_resolve`, `mean_attempts_to_resolve`, and `helix_triggered` counts to CSV.

### 2. 100% Visual Architecture Coverage (`115/115` Lessons)
- Every single lesson (`115/115`, `100%`) embeds a custom `<aside class="novak-visual-blueprint">` containing:
  1. A 5-stage inline SVG signal/architecture diagram.
  2. A 5-row RFC/IEEE/hardware `<table class="novak-spec-table">` technical reference table.
  3. An interactive `<details class="novak-field-watchout">` field technician watchout.
- Supplemented by `10` full-width multi-layer annotated SVG architecture diagrams. Zero plain-text walls.

### 3. Hands-On Browser Labs (`105` Total Labs / `98` Interactive Browser Labs, `8` Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME GUI + Bash Split-View Workbenches, `24` Real Linux VMs, `90` Core Catalog Baseline)
- **`105` total hands-on labs (`98` interactive browser labs + `9` classroom labs, expanding the `90` browser-based interactive labs baseline)** requiring zero local installation or external cloud VM popups:
  - **`8` Ubuntu 24.04 LTS GNOME 46 Desktop + Bash Split-View Workbenches (`linuxgui`)**: `linux-gui-network` (NetworkManager IPv4/DNS), `linux-gui-disks` (GNOME Disks, SMART & `/etc/fstab`), `linux-gui-firewall` (GUFW Firewall & systemd daemons), `linux-gui-users` (GNOME Users, sudo & Nautilus permissions), `linux-gui-logs` (GNOME Logs / `journalctl` brute-force triage & Fail2Ban), `linux-gui-processes` (GNOME System Monitor runaway PID & `vm.swappiness`), `linux-gui-packages` (Ubuntu Software APT & `/etc/crontab` scheduler), and `linux-gui-ssh` (GNOME Passwords & Keys `seahorse` Ed25519 + `sshd_config` hardening). Every Linux lesson leads with a GUI + Bash Split-View workbench.
  - **`24` real in-browser Linux VMs** (Alpine/x86 WebAssembly Linux 6.8 VM with a live root shell, filesystem, `/proc`, networking utilities, and an embedded Ubuntu GNOME GUI Split-View Companion bar).
  - **`66` stateful Windows 11, Cisco IOS & Hardware labs** (`8` Windows 11 GUI desktop labs, `27` Windows PowerShell/CMD labs, `19` Cisco IOS Switch & Router CLI labs covering `VLANs`, `802.1Q trunks`, `ROAS`, `OSPF`, `ACLs`, `NAT`, and `9` interactive drag-and-drop hardware/subnetting workbenches).
- **Process-Based Grading (`Diagnose → Fix → Verify`)**: Every lab grades whether the student ran diagnostic telemetry before applying a fix and verified service restoration afterward—preventing blind guessing.

### 4. Exam-Day Simulator & 3-Tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbench
- **`1,400` unique scenario-based items** mapped across `100%` of the `98` official sub-objectives:
  - `220-1201 A+ Core 1`: `466` unique scenario items + `10` interactive simulation PBQs.
  - `220-1202 A+ Core 2`: `463` unique scenario items + `10` interactive simulation PBQs.
  - `N10-009 Network+`: `454` unique scenario items + `10` interactive simulation PBQs.
  - `FC0-U71 Tech+`: `660` unique scenario items + `6` interactive simulation PBQs.
- **`36` Multi-Part Interactive Simulation PBQs** powered by a **3-Tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbench**:
  1. *Topology & Hardware Visualizer (SVG)*: Clickable network topologies (`Core Router`, `L2/L3 Switch`, `Firewall/DMZ`, `RADIUS/DNS`, `WLC/APs`), hardware bays (`PCIe/DIMM/M.2`, `PSU Rails`, `Laser Imaging Assembly`, `RJ-45/Fiber Patch Panel`), and OS/Security pipelines (`UEFI/GPT`, `NTFS/POSIX`, `GPO/Service`) with live green configured badges (`✓`).
  2. *Live Device Inspector / Logs*: Contextual `show interfaces trunk`, `show ip ospf neighbor`, `SMART/POST`, `bcdedit /enum`, `icacls`, and `ls -la` telemetry per node with 1-click jump to config fields.
  3. *Diagnostic Terminal (`pbq-cli`)*: Working in-browser diagnostic console supporting `help`, `status`, `show run`, `show vlan`, `show ip route`, `ping`, `nslookup`, `ipconfig /all`, `diskpart`, `bootrec`, `permissions`, and `inspect <row>`.
- **Authentic Sitting Controls**: `100–900` scaled scoring, `VOUCHER READY` certification gate (`2` consecutive sittings `>= 780`), digital scratch whiteboard, option strikethrough, mark-for-review, and ADA extended-time accommodations (`1.25x`, `1.5x`, `2.0x`).

### 5. Proctored Course Assessments & Rapid Recall
- **`405` Proctored Knowledge Test scenario questions** standardized at **`45` questions per form across Forms A, B, and C** (`135` per course across `ITSUP`, `NETOPS`, and `CLIENT`).
- **`26` Chapter Quizzes** (`230` unique chapter quiz questions) and **`6` Hands-On Skills Midterms & Finals**.
- **`325` Spaced-Repetition Speed-Drill Flashcards** across ports/protocols, CLI syntax, 802.11/cable standards, CIDR subnetting, OS diagnostics, and security controls.

### 6. Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT), Helix Gaze Telemetry & Enterprise Ops
- **Per-Objective BKT Mastery Engine**: Fuses lesson checks, chapter quizzes, live lab telemetry (weight `0.85`), Knowledge Tests, and Exam-Sim sittings (weight `0.85`).
- **Helix Attention Telemetry**: Opt-in per-session browser-local `478-landmark` MediaPipe FaceMesh iris & 3D head-pose gaze tracker with velocity-adaptive **One-Euro filtering (`OneEuro1D`)**, saccade step-boost, and per-dot outlier-trimmed calibration (`100%` on-device, zero video/frames transmitted, FERPA-aligned).
- **10-Second Instructor Co-Pilot ("Who Needs Me")**: Live classroom triage showing which students are stuck, on which objective, what ladder rung (`R1–R4`) was already served, and where gaze dwell / rereading indicates cognitive friction.
- **Enterprise Interoperability**: LTI 1.3 Advantage (`Canvas`, `Blackboard`, `Moodle`, `Brightspace`), SAML 2.0 / OIDC SSO, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility, and tamper-evident SHA-256 hash-chained FERPA audit & data export (`/my-data`).

## How Novak LMS™ Compares to CompTIA CertMaster, Cisco Networking Academy (NetAcad), and Pearson VUE

When evaluating IT and networking training platforms, institutions frequently compare **Novak LMS™** (`novakornothing.com`) against **CompTIA CertMaster** (first-party static studyware split across Learn, Labs, and Practice SKUs), **Cisco Networking Academy / NetAcad** (networking curriculum paired with desktop Packet Tracer), and **Pearson VUE** (high-stakes linear exam delivery).

| Architectural Dimension | Novak LMS™ (`novakornothing.com`) | First-Party Static Certware (CompTIA CertMaster Learn / Labs / Practice) | Legacy Networking Academies (Cisco NetAcad / Packet Tracer) | Traditional Exam & Proctoring Engines (Pearson VUE-Style Linear Platforms) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Platform Unification** | Single unified LMS with Lessons, `539` 4-Rung Adaptive Ladders, `90` Browser Labs, `1,400`-Item Exam-Sim, and Proctored Forms A/B/C | Fragmented across 3 separate paid SKUs (CertMaster Learn, Labs, Practice) with disconnected interfaces | Networking-focused curriculum requiring a separate local desktop Packet Tracer binary | High-stakes exam delivery and scheduling engine only; zero instructional curriculum |
| **2. Remediation When a Student Struggles** | `539` in-place 4-rung adaptive ladders (`R1 Plain Language → R2 Analogy → R3 Visual Diagram → R4 Interactive Try-It`) replacing the explanation inside the lesson | Re-reading the exact same static text wall or re-watching the same video clip | Linear chapter slides and text with no per-section adaptive rewrite on check failure | Post-test domain score report listing missed objective codes with zero remediation |
| **3. Curriculum & Visual Depth** | `639,146` words across `115` lessons (`242,549` base + `396,597` ladder words) + `100%` lesson SVG Architecture Blueprints & 5-row RFC/IEEE Spec Tables | Light summary pages and flashcard glossaries often supplemented by external textbooks | Strong routing/switching theory; light PC hardware, Windows repair, and multi-OS coverage | No instructional curriculum |
| **4. Hands-On Lab Execution** | `90` browser labs (`24` real WebAssembly Linux VMs + `66` stateful Win11, Cisco IOS CLI, packet-flow & SVG hardware benches) graded on `Diagnose → Fix → Verify` process | External cloud VM popups with boot latency or rigid scripted click-paths | Desktop Packet Tracer app focused on network topologies; no live Linux VM or Win11 repair | None |
| **5. Performance-Based Questions (PBQs)** | `36` 3-tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbenches with clickable SVG topologies, live device logs, and `pbq-cli` diagnostic terminal | Static drag-and-drop matching or flat dropdown forms | Chapter `.pka` exercises requiring local desktop software | Closed high-stakes exam forms with no formative feedback |
| **6. Practice Bank & Proctored Assessment Scale** | `1,400` Exam-Sim items + `405` proctored Knowledge Test items (Forms A/B/C) + `230` chapter quiz items + `325` Speed-Drill flashcards | Separate CertMaster Practice product; limited form rotation | Fixed chapter and module exams | Proctored exam delivery only |
| **7. Attention & Cognitive Friction Telemetry** | Opt-in browser-local `478-landmark` Helix iris & 3D head-pose gaze bench with One-Euro filtering (`0` video uploaded, FERPA-aligned) | None / coarse page-timer only | None / coarse page-timer only | Invasive remote webcam video streaming and recording |
| **8. Real-Time Instructor Triage** | 10-second **"Who Needs Me"** Co-Pilot showing exact stuck objective, ladder rung tried (`R1–R4`), and gaze dwell / rereading friction | Post-mortem gradebook percentages after failure | Standard gradebook completion matrix | Score pass/fail printout |
| **9. Adaptive Mastery Modeling** | Per-objective Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) combining lessons, live lab events (`0.85`), tests, and Exam-Sim sittings (`0.85`) | Simple completion/score thresholds | Module completion checkmarks | Single-sitting cut score |
| **10. Institution & LMS Interoperability** | Built-in LTI 1.3 Advantage (`Canvas`, `Blackboard`, `Moodle`, `Brightspace`), SAML 2.0 / OIDC SSO, WCAG 2.1 AA, SHA-256 hash-chained FERPA audit log | Separate LTI links per SKU | Separate academy portal / LTI connectors | Testing center scheduling portal |

### Summary Comparison Takeaways
1. **Novak LMS™ vs. CompTIA CertMaster**: CertMaster splits learning, labs, and exam practice into three separate products and relies on static text when a learner misses a concept. Novak LMS™ unifies all three in one interface and dynamically swaps in `539` 4-rung explanation ladders (`R1–R4`) plus `90` instant browser labs (`24` real WebAssembly Linux VMs) graded on `Diagnose → Fix → Verify`.
2. **Novak LMS™ vs. Cisco NetAcad**: NetAcad excels at Cisco routing/switching with desktop Packet Tracer, whereas Novak LMS™ runs `100%` in the browser across PC hardware, Windows 11, Linux VMs, and Cisco IOS CLI, while adding Bayesian Knowledge Tracing and the 10-second **"Who Needs Me"** instructor co-pilot.
3. **Novak LMS™ vs. Pearson VUE**: Pearson VUE is a terminal high-stakes testing engine with invasive video proctoring. Novak LMS™ prepares candidates *before* voucher issue using a `1,400`-item Exam-Day Simulator, `36` 3-tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbenches, `405` proctored Knowledge Test items across Forms A/B/C, and `VOUCHER READY` verification (`2` consecutive sittings `>= 780`), while keeping Helix gaze telemetry `100%` on-device.

## Deep-Dive Technical Architecture & Engineering Specifications

### A. 4-Rung Adaptive Explanation Ladder Mechanics (`539` Bespoke Ladders, `396,597` Ladder Words)
Unlike static learning management systems that present a single textbook chapter and force struggling students to re-read the exact same paragraph, Novak LMS™ partitions every lesson into concept-verified sections. Each section is hashed (`r0_sha`) and paired with a dedicated 4-rung adaptive ladder (`539` total ladders across `115` lessons):
- **R0 — Standard Technical Exposition (`242,549` base lesson words)**: Authoritative engineering prose featuring an embedded `<aside class="novak-visual-blueprint">` (5-stage inline SVG signal/architecture diagram + 5-row RFC/IEEE/hardware `<table class="novak-spec-table">` + interactive `<details class="novak-field-watchout">`).
- **R1 — Plain Language Rewrite**: Triggered automatically when a student misses the ungraded section check. Strips dense acronym stacking and re-explains the mechanism using direct operational cause-and-effect language.
- **R2 — Concrete Analogy**: Triggered on a second miss. Maps protocol handshakes, OS kernel structures, or electrical tolerances onto physical shop/logistics systems while preserving strict technical accuracy.
- **R3 — Visual Diagram Walk-Through**: Triggered on a third miss. Breaks the signal path, packet header, or boot chain into numbered visual stages so spatial learners can trace the fault boundary.
- **R4 — Interactive Hands-On Try-It**: Triggered on a fourth miss (or on demand). Embeds an interactive fault-isolation micro-exercise directly inside the lesson section.
- **Instructor Visibility ("What Finally Clicked")**: Every rung transition and resolution is logged per student and aggregated across the cohort so instructors can see which explanation style (`R1`, `R2`, `R3`, or `R4`) unlocked mastery for each individual learner.

### B. 3-Tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbench (`36` Multi-Part Simulation PBQs)
Every certification sitting in the Novak LMS™ Exam-Day Simulator begins with multi-part Performance-Based Questions (PBQs) modeled on real field incidents. All `36` PBQs (`10` for `220-1201 A+ Core 1`, `10` for `220-1202 A+ Core 2`, `10` for `N10-009 Network+`, and `6` for `FC0-U71 Tech+`) execute inside the **3-Tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbench**:
1. **Tab 1 — Topology & Hardware Visualizer (Interactive SVG)**:
   - Renders clickable enterprise network topologies (`Core Router`, `L2/L3 Distribution Switch`, `Firewall/DMZ`, `RADIUS/DNS Server`, `WLC/APs`), physical PC/server hardware bays (`PCIe/DIMM/M.2 slots`, `24-pin/EPS12V PSU rails`, `7-step Laser Imaging Assembly`, `RJ-45/Fiber Patch Panels`), and OS/Security pipelines (`UEFI/GPT boot chain`, `NTFS/POSIX permissions`, `GPO/Service recovery`).
   - Clicking any SVG node selects the device, highlights its live telemetry, and displays green configured badges (`✓`) as remediation parameters are locked in.
2. **Tab 2 — Live Device Inspector / Logs**:
   - Exposes authentic per-node telemetry outputs including `show interfaces trunk`, `show ip ospf neighbor`, `show vlan brief`, `SMART/POST` diagnostic codes, `bcdedit /enum`, `icacls`, `systemctl status`, and `ls -la`.
   - Includes 1-click jump links from anomalous log lines directly to the corresponding remediation configuration control.
3. **Tab 3 — Diagnostic Terminal (`pbq-cli`)**:
   - A working in-browser command-line diagnostic console supporting `help`, `status`, `show run`, `show vlan`, `show ip route`, `ping`, `nslookup`, `ipconfig /all`, `diskpart`, `bootrec`, `permissions`, and `inspect <row>`.

### 220-1201 CompTIA A+ Core 1 Interactive Simulation PBQs (`10` Workbench Scenarios)
1. **`SIM-A1-1` (Objective `A1:2.1`)**: Terminate a straight-through patch cable to the T568B standard. Inspect the pinout card, then choose the colour for each pin.
2. **`SIM-A1-2` (Objective `A1:3.4`)**: A technician installs an M.2 NVMe SSD and a second RAM kit, but the new SSD does not appear as a boot option. Inspect the board, then fix the build.
3. **`SIM-A1-3` (Objective `A1:5.3`)**: A laptop shows "Limited" Wi-Fi in a hotel. Run the read-only checks, then pick the fix.
4. **`SIM-A1-4` (Objective `A1:5.6`)**: Accounting users report that every page from the departmental laser printer has loose toner that smears when touched and faint ghost images down the page. Inspect the printer status and service it.
5. **`SIM-A1-5` (Objective `A1:5.1`)**: A newly assembled CAD workstation powers on, fans spin at 100%, and the motherboard emits 1 long and 2 short beeps with a blank monitor. Inspect the build and resolve the POST fault.
6. **`SIM-A1-6` (Objective `A1:5.2`)**: A small file server running a 4-disk RAID 5 array beeps and reports degraded performance. Inspect the storage controller and recover redundancy without losing data.
7. **`SIM-A1-7` (Objective `A1:1.3`)**: A travelling executive cannot receive corporate email on an iPhone after a password rotation, and MDM shows the device out of compliance. Inspect the MDM console and restore access.
8. **`SIM-A1-8` (Objective `A1:4.1`)**: A developer tries to start two 64-bit Linux VMs in Hyper-V on a workstation, but the hypervisor refuses to start the VMs and the second VM fails with an out-of-memory error. Inspect the host and fix both issues.
9. **`SIM-A1-9` (Objective `A1:2.5`)**: Two new PoE+ PTZ security cameras (24 W each) connected to an 8-port PoE switch keep rebooting whenever their pan/tilt motors engage. Inspect the switch PoE budget and fix the installation.
10. **`SIM-A1-10` (Objective `A1:5.4`)**: A field technician’s tablet trackpad cursor jumps erratically and the bottom bezel is lifting away from the aluminum frame. Inspect the device diagnostics and choose the safe procedure.

### 220-1202 CompTIA A+ Core 2 Interactive Simulation PBQs (`10` Workbench Scenarios)
1. **`SIM-A2-1` (Objective `A2:1.6`)**: Remote Desktop to PC-FIN07 fails from the help desk. Inspect the services and firewall, then configure the PC.
2. **`SIM-A2-2` (Objective `A2:3.1`)**: A user reports pop-ups and a browser homepage that keeps changing. Inspect the PC and order your response like the malware-removal process.
3. **`SIM-A2-3` (Objective `A2:2.6`)**: A shared folder must give the Finance group change access and everyone else no access. Inspect the effective permissions, then set them.
4. **`SIM-A2-4` (Objective `A2:3.1`)**: After a power outage, a Windows 11 workstation displays "BOOTMGR is missing / No bootable device" even though UEFI detects the NVMe SSD. Inspect the WinRE command prompt and repair the boot configuration.
5. **`SIM-A2-5` (Objective `A2:1.9`)**: A Linux web developer updated /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/app.conf, but the web server still serves the old config and a backup script /opt/scripts/backup.sh fails with "Permission denied". Fix both issues.
6. **`SIM-A2-6` (Objective `A2:1.5`)**: Domain workstations in the Accounting OU can ping servers by IP (10.20.1.10) but fail to resolve internal hostnames after a DNS migration, and a new logon banner GPO has not yet applied. Inspect the client and fix it.
7. **`SIM-A2-7` (Objective `A2:2.7`)**: A lost corporate laptop was recovered, and an audit revealed that a shared local Administrator account with no lockout policy and an unencrypted SSD were in use. Harden the workstation to policy.
8. **`SIM-A2-8` (Objective `A2:4.2`)**: An administrator pushed a registry script directly to 400 production call-center PCs at 10:30 AM without testing or approval, breaking the softphone app. Review the change record and enforce change management.
9. **`SIM-A2-9` (Objective `A2:1.8`)**: A graphic designer’s MacBook Pro (macOS Sonoma) becomes unresponsive while exporting a project, and Time Machine reports that backups have not completed in 42 days. Inspect the Mac and resolve both issues.
10. **`SIM-A2-10` (Objective `A2:2.11`)**: A remote bookkeeper reports certificate warnings on every banking site and unexpected search redirects in Chrome. Inspect the browser and Windows proxy settings to clean up the hijacker.

### N10-009 CompTIA Network+ Interactive Simulation PBQs (`10` Workbench Scenarios)
1. **`SIM-N-1` (Objective `N:2.2`)**: Users on PC-B (VLAN 20) cannot reach the file server in VLAN 10, but PC-A (VLAN 10) can. Inspect the switch, then fix the fault.
2. **`SIM-N-2` (Objective `N:5.5`)**: A branch PC (192.168.50.20) cannot browse https://intranet (10.1.1.80). Ping works. Use the router tabs to find and fix the fault.
3. **`SIM-N-3` (Objective `N:1.7`)**: A new hire's laptop shows 169.254.x.x while every other host on the same subnet works. Inspect the host, then correct its settings.
4. **`SIM-N-4` (Objective `N:2.2`)**: Switches SW-CORE and SW-ACC1 have two redundant gigabit links bundled into Port-channel 1, but the bundle is down and spanning tree blocks both ports as err-disabled/suspended. Inspect both switches and fix the LACP trunk.
5. **`SIM-N-5` (Objective `N:2.1`)**: Router R1 and R2 share a point-to-point subnet (10.0.12.0/30) in OSPF Area 0, but the adjacency never forms. Inspect the OSPF outputs and resolve the mismatch.
6. **`SIM-N-6` (Objective `N:3.4`)**: Workstations in VLAN 30 (10.30.0.0/24) obtain 169.254.x.x addresses even though the central DHCP server (10.100.0.50) has an active scope for 10.30.0.0/24. Inspect the distribution router and fix DHCP relay.
7. **`SIM-N-7` (Objective `N:2.3`)**: Clients on the 2nd floor experience frequent drops and high retries on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. Inspect the wireless controller survey and fix the channel and security config.
8. **`SIM-N-8` (Objective `N:4.3`)**: An unauthorized hub was plugged into access port Gi0/12 on SW-IDF3, and a rogue DHCP server began handing out leases. Inspect the switch config and harden the access edge.
9. **`SIM-N-9` (Objective `N:5.2`)**: A newly patched 10GBASE-SR fiber link between SW-MDF and SW-IDF4 stays down/down. Inspect the transceiver DOM readings and patch panel notes to fix the link.
10. **`SIM-N-10` (Objective `N:3.2`)**: The NOC SIEM is not receiving syslog alerts from router R-EDGE, and SNMPv3 polling from the NMS (10.100.5.20) times out. Inspect R-EDGE and fix both monitoring feeds.

### FC0-U71 CompTIA Tech+ Interactive Simulation PBQs (`6` Workbench Scenarios)
1. **`SIM-T-1` (Objective `T:3.1`)**: A user on a shared Windows 11 workstation reports their system is sluggish and cannot save files to the D: data volume. Inspect the workstation and choose the remediation steps.
2. **`SIM-T-2` (Objective `T:6.1`)**: An office manager needs a secure wireless network for staff laptops and a separate guest network that cannot reach internal accounting servers. Review the router settings and complete the setup.
3. **`SIM-T-3` (Objective `T:1.2`)**: All 18 desktop PCs in Training Room B lost internet access at 9:00 AM, while Wi-Fi laptops in the hallway still work. Inspect the room switch and apply the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology.
4. **`SIM-T-4` (Objective `T:4.1`)**: An IT intern wrote a nightly PowerShell script to check free disk space and archive old log files, but the script never triggers the warning branch even when free space is 2 GB. Inspect the script and fix the logic bug.
5. **`SIM-T-5` (Objective `T:5.1`)**: A dental clinic’s patient scheduling database server suffered a drive failure on Wednesday at 2:00 PM. Review the backup schedule and SQL log to restore the database with minimal data loss.
6. **`SIM-T-6` (Objective `T:6.2`)**: An employee received an urgent email claiming to be from "IT Helpdesk <support@micros0ft-login-verify.com>" asking them to scan a QR code and enter their corporate password and MFA code. Analyze the incident and respond.

---

### C. Hands-On Browser Lab Engine (`90` Labs · `24` Real WebAssembly Linux VMs · `Diagnose → Fix → Verify`)
- **24 Real In-Browser Linux VMs**: Powered by an x86/Alpine WebAssembly virtual machine running entirely in the student's browser tab with root shell access, live `/etc` configuration files, systemd/service mocks, disk/mount tables, POSIX permissions, and network interface utilities (`ip`, `ss`, `ping`, `dig`, `iptables`, `grep`, `awk`, `chmod`, `chown`).
- **66 Stateful Multi-Domain Simulators**:
  - **Windows 11 Administration & Repair**: Stateful Windows 11 Settings, Disk Management, Event Viewer, Device Manager, Services, Group Policy, `cmd.exe`, and PowerShell (`ipconfig /flushdns`, `netsh int ip reset`, `sfc /scannow`, `DISM`, `bcdedit`, `bootrec`, `chkdsk`).
  - **Cisco IOS Switch & Router CLI**: Full user exec, privileged exec (`enable`), global configuration (`configure terminal`), interface configuration (`switchport mode trunk`, `switchport trunk allowed vlan`, `ip address`, `no shutdown`), sub-interface 802.1Q encapsulation (`encapsulation dot1Q`), OSPF routing, standard/extended ACLs, and NVRAM persistence (`write memory` / `copy running-config startup-config`).
  - **Interactive Packet-Flow & Hardware Workbenches**: Visual packet tracer across L2/L3 hops, DNS/DHCP DORA animators, and ESD/motherboard/PSU fault isolation benches.
- **Process-Verified Grading (`Diagnose → Fix → Verify`)**:
  - **Stage 1 (Diagnose)**: Verifies that the learner inspected telemetry (e.g., `show interfaces trunk`, `ipconfig /all`, `systemctl status`, voltage rail check) before modifying state.
  - **Stage 2 (Fix)**: Evaluates the exact configuration or hardware remediation applied.
  - **Stage 3 (Verify)**: Confirms the learner executed a post-fix verification command (`ping`, `nslookup`, `show ip route`, reboot verification) proving operational recovery.

---

### D. Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) & Helix One-Euro Gaze Telemetry Pipeline
- **Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) Parameters & Evidence Weights**:
  - Maintains a continuous posterior mastery probability $P(L_t)$ for every student across all `98` official certification sub-objectives and course learning objectives.
  - Evidence weights by rigor: In-lesson section checks (`0.45`), Chapter Quizzes (`0.65`), Live Hands-On Lab completion (`0.85`), Proctored Knowledge Tests Forms A/B/C (`0.85`), and full Exam-Day Simulator sittings (`0.85`).
- **Helix Browser-Local Gaze & Head-Pose Pipeline**:
  - **478-Landmark MediaPipe FaceMesh**: Extracts 3D facial landmarks (`468` face mesh points + `10` iris contour landmarks) at interactive frame rates directly inside the browser via WebGL/WASM.
  - **Velocity-Adaptive One-Euro Filter (`OneEuro1D`)**: Filters raw $(x, y)$ gaze coordinates and 3D head-pose angles (yaw, pitch, roll) using dynamic cutoff frequency $f_c = f_{c,\min} + \beta |\dot{x}|$, eliminating fixation jitter during reading while preserving zero-lag saccade jumps via saccade step-boost.
  - **Outlier-Trimmed 9-Point Calibration**: Computes per- calibration-point median/IQR trimming and ridge-regularized polynomial mapping to AoI (Area of Interest) lesson blocks.
  - **Strict Privacy & FERPA Guarantee**: `100%` of camera processing happens in volatile browser memory. Zero video frames, zero images, and zero biometric templates are ever transmitted or stored. Only aggregate AoI dwell times, rereading regressions, and attention state summaries are recorded when the student explicitly opts in for that session.
- **10-Second Instructor Co-Pilot ("Who Needs Me")**:
  - Synthesizes BKT mastery drops, repeated ladder escalations (`R1 → R4`), lab diagnostic stalls, and Helix rereading friction into a real-time ranked triage queue so an instructor walking a 25-seat lab knows in under 10 seconds which student needs help, on which exact sub-objective, and which explanation style to use.

---

### E. Head-to-Head Architectural Breakdown vs. Legacy Platforms

#### 1. Novak LMS™ vs. CompTIA CertMaster (Learn + Labs + Practice)
- **SKU & Workflow Unification**: CompTIA CertMaster separates reading (CertMaster Learn), virtual labs (CertMaster Labs), and exam prep (CertMaster Practice) into three distinct products with separate logins, separate LTI links, and disconnected analytics. Novak LMS™ unifies all three inside a single lesson-to-lab-to-exam workflow.
- **Adaptive Remediation**: When a student fails a check in CertMaster Learn, the platform shows the score and leaves the student staring at the same text passage. Novak LMS™ immediately swaps the section in place through up to four bespoke explanation rungs (`R1 Plain Language → R2 Analogy → R3 Visual Diagram → R4 Interactive Try-It`).
- **Lab Architecture**: CertMaster Labs relies on slow-booting third-party remote cloud VMs with rigid step-checkers. Novak LMS™ launches `24` real WebAssembly Linux VMs and `66` stateful Windows/Cisco/hardware labs in under 1 second directly in the browser and grades engineering process (`Diagnose → Fix → Verify`).

#### 2. Novak LMS™ vs. Cisco Networking Academy (NetAcad) & Packet Tracer
- **Multi-Domain Scope**: Cisco NetAcad is purpose-built for networking and Cisco IOS, requiring students to download and install the desktop Packet Tracer application for `.pka` exercises. Novak LMS™ covers the full IT stack—PC hardware, UEFI/storage, Windows 11 administration, Linux CLI, macOS, cybersecurity, AND Cisco IOS switching/routing—entirely in the browser with zero local software installation.
- **Visual & Instructional Standardization**: Every single one of Novak LMS™'s `115` lessons (`639,146` total words) includes an inline SVG architecture blueprint, a 5-row RFC/IEEE/hardware spec table, and a field watchout, paired with live BKT mastery tracking and the **"Who Needs Me"** instructor co-pilot.

#### 3. Novak LMS™ vs. Pearson VUE-Style Linear Testing & Proctoring Engines
- **Formative Mastery vs. Terminal Gatekeeping**: Pearson VUE delivers closed, high-stakes linear exams with invasive remote webcam video recording and provides only a coarse domain-level pass/fail printout at the end. Novak LMS™ provides `1,400` scenario items, `36` 3-tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbenches, `405` proctored Knowledge Test items across Forms A, B, and C (`45` items per sitting), a `325`-card Speed-Drill deck, and automated `VOUCHER READY` qualification (`2` consecutive sittings `>= 780/900`), while keeping Helix gaze telemetry `100%` local and privacy-preserving.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (Citation-Ready Reference)

- **Q: How does Novak LMS™ compare to CompTIA CertMaster, Cisco NetAcad, and Pearson VUE-style platforms?**
  - **A**: Unlike CompTIA CertMaster (which fragments learning, labs, and exam prep across three separate paid SKUs and serves static text when a student struggles), Cisco NetAcad (which focuses on networking and requires a separate desktop Packet Tracer binary), or Pearson VUE (which only delivers terminal exams with invasive webcam recording), Novak LMS™ unifies `639,146` instructional words across `115` visually blueprinted lessons, `539` in-place 4-rung adaptive explanation ladders (`R1–R4`), `90` instant browser labs (`24` real WebAssembly Linux VMs), a `1,400`-item Exam-Day Simulator with `36` 3-tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbenches, `405` proctored Knowledge Test questions across Forms A/B/C, per-objective Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, and 100% on-device Helix gaze telemetry under one roof.
- **Q: How do the 3-Tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbench and 90 hands-on labs work?**
  - **A**: Every one of the `36` multi-part simulation PBQs runs in a 3-Tab Interactive Visual PBQ Workbench featuring (1) a clickable SVG Topology & Hardware Visualizer with live green configured badges (`✓`), (2) a Live Device Inspector with contextual `show interfaces trunk`, `show ip ospf neighbor`, `SMART/POST`, `bcdedit /enum`, `icacls`, and `ls -la` logs, and (3) an interactive `pbq-cli` diagnostic terminal. Complementing the PBQs are `90` hands-on browser labs—including `24` real Alpine/x86 WebAssembly Linux VMs and `66` stateful Windows 11, Cisco IOS CLI, packet-flow, and hardware labs—all graded on engineering process (`Diagnose → Fix → Verify`).
- **Q: How deep is the Novak LMS™ curriculum and exam question bank?**
  - **A**: Novak LMS™ spans `3` full courses (`Client Systems / FC0-U71`, `IT Support / 220-1201 & 220-1202`, and `Network Operations / N10-009`), `26` chapters, and `115` lessons totaling `242,549` base lesson words and `639,146` total instructional words (including `396,597` words across `539` 4-rung explanation ladders). Every lesson (`115/115`, `100%`) embeds a 5-stage SVG visual blueprint, a 5-row RFC/IEEE/hardware spec table, and a field watchout. Assessments include `1,400` Exam-Sim items (`466` for `220-1201`, `463` for `220-1202`, `454` for `N10-009`, `660` for `FC0-U71`), `36` interactive PBQs, `405` proctored Knowledge Test items (`45` per Form A/B/C across 3 courses), `230` chapter quiz items across `26` quizzes, `6` Skills Midterms/Finals, and `325` Speed-Drill flashcards.
- **Q: How does Novak LMS™ combine Helix eye tracking and Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) for instructors?**
  - **A**: Novak LMS™ pairs a per-objective Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) mastery model (weighting lesson checks, quizzes, live labs at `0.85`, Knowledge Tests, and Exam-Sim sittings at `0.85`) with Helix, an opt-in browser-local `478-landmark` MediaPipe FaceMesh iris and 3D head-pose tracker using velocity-adaptive One-Euro filtering (`OneEuro1D`). Zero video or images ever leave the student's device. The 10-second **"Who Needs Me"** Instructor Co-Pilot fuses these signals to show which students are stuck, on which exact objective, which ladder rung (`R1–R4`) was already served, and where gaze dwell or rereading indicates cognitive friction.
